title: Check the scope labels first
statement: Check every scope label against the official framework before an item is made or judged, pass it explicitly and unchanged through every step, and confirm how the judge reads it.
example: One wrong period mapping in a generator's settings caused 77 curriculum-alignment hard-fails, the majority of all failures in its baseline.
detail: In one quality push on an AP question generator, its settings mapped several units to the wrong period, so items matched their topic but carried the wrong time period, and the evaluator hard-failed them on curriculum alignment (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark/CHANGELOG_RELENTLESS.md`). That single settings error caused 77 hard-fails in the baseline, the majority of all failures. The evaluator in turn returned systematically wrong unit numbers for one course's standards, so the generator corrected them before evaluation (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/CHANGELOG.md`). The labels are the course, unit, period, standard and procedure. Match them to the framework by content, and pass them along as given.
against: The ID shift stayed in one source: an audit of 30 records of the canonical source found no shift in the affected course (0 of 10 records), though one record there carried a wrong unit (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_grader_audit_results_2_of_3_pass.md`, lines 22-26). That a wrong ID makes the grader fail correct content is the note's reasoning, not a measurement. The label fault was not the whole story: the report first put a 43-point fall on one item type (69 % → 26 %) down to a change in how the judge enforced the label, but the full run found the fault steady and touching only 27 of that type's 193 scored items, too few to account for most of the fall. the metadata-confirmed conflict rests on declared operation metadata, not an independent content adjudication (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/handoffs-2026-07-13/course-eval-layer/README.md`). The handover's techniques come from a sibling generator whose best run used a different grader version, which it calls design evidence, not certified current scores. a date-only screen mostly raised false alarms: 12 of the 18 records it flagged belonged where they were. The 70.7%-to-94.0% gain is cumulative over several commits, not all of them about the default. The fix carried the labels through and still falls back to parsing the code when no label is passed, so stopping on an unknown label is the lesson drawn, not the change measured (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark/CHANGELOG_RELENTLESS.md`). The exact-ID hit rate is second-hand: a 40-standard check "reportedly found 100% hit rate" (`ap_social_studies_generator_distilled.md`, line 68).

evidence.quote: Every generated item for these units had content matching the TOPIC but metadata saying the wrong TIME PERIOD. The evaluator saw the mismatch and issued automatic curriculum_alignment hard-fails.
**Impact:** 77 curriculum_alignment hard-fails in baseline. This single config error was responsible for the majority of all failures.
4. **APWH unit correction.** The evaluator returns systematically wrong unit numbers for APWH standards — we fix them before evaluation.
Every APEURO Unit 4 question automatically failed `curriculum_alignment` because the generated content referenced 1648-1815 material but the evaluator expected 1914-present content.

**Why this is significant:** No amount of prompt engineering can fix wrong metadata. The metadata (time period string) appears in every prompt for every question of that unit. Every question was doomed before generation started.
**Impact:** All APEURO Unit 4 questions went from 0% to baseline pass rate (~80%) instantly. This single change accounted for roughly 3-4% of the 15% total improvement.

**Why this was missed:** The code was doing "clever" re-derivation of course/unit from substandard_id. The problem with re-derivation: KC-prefixed standards are APWH-specific notation that the parser didn't handle. Passing explicit values eliminates the re-derivation entirely.
**Problem:** Question frames settlement houses as a Gilded Age phenomenon when the curriculum explicitly states they were Progressive Era (1890s-1920s). The Gilded Age ended around 1898.

`parse_substandard("KC-4.1.VI+1+D")` in the generator code doesn't match any of the regex patterns for course detection (USH/WH/EH/MAC/MIC/GOV/HG/EURO prefix). It silently falls through to the default: `{course="APUSH", unit=1}`.
So `ctx.course` came back as "APUSH" for all APWH items. Because `ctx.course != "APWH"`, the `_build_apwh_unit_guidance()` function added in commit 2 was **silently skipped** for every APWH request.
APWH u3 going from 43.3% to 100% with 0 hard-fails is the definitive proof that the KC-prefix routing chain (commits 3+4+2) was the root cause.
